name: SBI Clerk
fullName: State Bank of India – Junior Associates (Customer Support & Sales) Recruitment
conductingBody: State Bank of India (Central Recruitment & Promotion Department)
eligibility: Graduate in any discipline; 20–28 years as on 1 Apr 2026 (relaxation for reserved categories); knowledge of the local language of the state applied for

notification.summary: SBI Junior Associate 2026 (Advt. CRPD/CR/2026-27/17, ≈7,680 regular vacancies, plus a separate SC/ST/OBC backlog drive CRPD/CR/SPLDRIVE/2026-27/16) closed registration on 31 Aug 2026. Regular prelims were held on 26–27 Sep 2026; the prelims result is awaited and mains is tentatively in late Nov 2026. Figures are from news/job portals (vacancy counts vary between sources); the SBI careers page could not be opened from the research environment.

importantDates.event: Local Language Proficiency Test / final result

pattern.notes: 20 minutes per section with separate timers. No sectional cut-off; state- and category-wise overall cut-off. Prelims is qualifying only; final selection is on mains marks (190 Qs/200 marks) followed by a local language test.

trendAnalysis.summary: SBI Clerk prelims is easy-to-moderate with good attempts usually in the 70s. Numerical Ability is mostly speed-based: 10–15 simplification/approximation questions, a missing/wrong-number series, one DI set and short arithmetic problems. Reasoning has 3–4 small puzzles (linear row with vacant seats, floor-colour, box, day-based) worth 12–15 questions plus syllogism, inequality, coding, blood relations, direction and alphanumeric series. English centres on one RC (7–10 Qs), cloze, error spotting, fillers and sentence rearrangement; spelling and connector questions appear occasionally.

resources.notes: SBI does not publish Junior Associate question papers or answer keys. The official advertisement (with exam pattern) and pre-examination training material for eligible candidates are on sbi.bank.in/web/careers. Previous papers circulating online are memory-based compilations by coaching portals.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.

Millets were once a staple across much of India, but after the Green Revolution they were steadily replaced by rice and wheat, which received assured procurement and gave higher yields. Millets, however, need far less water, tolerate heat and grow well on poor soils. As groundwater levels fall and summers grow hotter, these qualities have attracted fresh attention. Several states now include millets in school meals and public distribution, hoping to create steady demand. Farmers say that demand alone is not enough: they also need better seeds, processing units close to villages and fair prices. Without these, they argue, millets will remain a niche product admired in seminars but rarely seen on dinner plates.

Why were millets replaced by rice and wheat after the Green Revolution?
options: Millets could not grow on poor soils
Rice and wheat had assured procurement and higher yields
Millets were banned from public distribution
questions.explanation: The passage says rice and wheat 'received assured procurement and gave higher yields'.

questions.question:
Read the passage and choose the word that best fits the numbered blank.

Online shopping festivals offer attractive discounts, but shoppers should remain (1) ______. Fraudsters often create fake websites that (2) ______ well-known brands. Before paying, customers should check the web address carefully and (3) ______ clicking on links received from unknown numbers.

Which word best fits blank (1)?
questions.explanation: Because frauds are common, shoppers should remain cautious.

Which word best fits blank (2)?
questions.explanation: Fake websites imitate (copy the look of) well-known brands.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
She did not knew (A)/ that the branch (B)/ would remain closed (C)/ on Saturday. (D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation: After 'did', the base form is used: 'did not know'. Error in part A.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
My brother, who lives in Pune, (A)/ is elder than (B)/ me by three years (C)/ and works in a bank. (D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation: 'Elder' is not followed by 'than'; the correct form is 'older than'. Error in part B.

questions.question:
Choose the word that best fills the blank.
The train was ______ by two hours due to dense fog.
questions.explanation: Fog causes a delay: 'The train was delayed by two hours'.

questions.question:
Choose the pair that best fills the blanks.
The manager ______ the proposal because it was not ______ with the bank's policy.
questions.explanation: A proposal not consistent with policy is rejected. 'Not accordance with' is ungrammatical, and accepting/welcoming contradicts 'because it was not…'.

questions.question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
A. He noticed that many elderly neighbours struggled to use mobile banking.
B. Arjun, a college student, spent his summer holidays at home.
C. So he started free weekend classes in the community hall.
D. By the end of the summer, over forty seniors could pay bills on their own.
E. Some of them even depended on strangers to complete simple payments.
questions.explanation: B (introduces Arjun) → A (what he noticed) → E (how bad it was) → C (his response) → D (result): BAECD.

questions.question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph and choose the LAST sentence.
A. Rinse the seeds and soak them overnight.
B. Next morning, drain the water and tie the seeds in a wet cloth.
C. Sprouts are a cheap and healthy addition to any meal.
D. Within a day or two, small shoots will appear.
E. Making them at home is simple.
questions.explanation: Order: C – E – A – B – D. The last sentence is D.

questions.question:
Choose the option that should replace the phrase in capitals.
Each of the players HAVE BEEN GIVEN a new kit.
questions.explanation: 'Each of the players' is singular and the sense is passive: 'has been given'.

questions.question:
Which pair of highlighted words should be interchanged to make the sentence correct?
The (A) house delivered the (B) letter to the wrong (C) address because the (D) postman number was unclear.
questions.explanation: Swapping A and D: 'The postman delivered the letter to the wrong address because the house number was unclear.'

questions.question: Choose the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Receive' (e before i after c).

questions.question:
Choose the connector that best joins the sentences: 'It was raining heavily. The match was not cancelled.'
______ it was raining heavily, the match was not cancelled.
questions.explanation: The ideas contrast (heavy rain, yet not cancelled), so 'Even though' fits.

Six persons G, H, I, J, K and L sit in a row of seven seats facing north; one seat is vacant. The vacant seat is third from the left end. H sits second to the right of the vacant seat. Only one seat lies between H and I. K sits next to I. L sits immediately to the right of the vacant seat. G does not sit at either end.

Who sits at the extreme left end?
questions.explanation: Seats 1–7 (left to right): J, G, vacant, L, H, K, I. Vacant = 3, L = 4, H = 5, I = 7 (seat 3 is vacant), K = 6; G is not at an end so G = 2 and J = 1.

questions.question:
Six persons G, H, I, J, K and L sit in a row of seven seats facing north; one seat is vacant. The vacant seat is third from the left end. H sits second to the right of the vacant seat. Only one seat lies between H and I. K sits next to I. L sits immediately to the right of the vacant seat. G does not sit at either end.

How many persons sit between G and K?
questions.explanation: Seats: J, G, vacant, L, H, K, I. Between G (2) and K (6) are seat 3 (vacant), L and H — two persons.

questions.question:
Six persons G, H, I, J, K and L sit in a row of seven seats facing north; one seat is vacant. The vacant seat is third from the left end. H sits second to the right of the vacant seat. Only one seat lies between H and I. K sits next to I. L sits immediately to the right of the vacant seat. G does not sit at either end.

Who sits immediately to the left of H?
questions.explanation: Seats: J, G, vacant, L, H, K, I. Facing north, left means the lower-numbered seat; L (seat 4) is immediately left of H (seat 5).

questions.question:
Five persons A, B, C, D and E live on five different floors of a building (floor 1 is the bottom, floor 5 the top), and each likes a different colour — Red, Blue, Green, White and Pink. B lives on the top floor. Only one person lives between B and A. D likes Blue and lives immediately below B. C lives on a floor below E. E likes Red. The one who likes Green lives on an odd-numbered floor above A. A does not like White.

Who likes Pink?
questions.explanation: Floors 1→5: C-White, E-Red, A-Pink, D-Blue, B-Green. A likes Pink.

questions.question:
Five persons A, B, C, D and E live on five different floors of a building (floor 1 is the bottom, floor 5 the top), and each likes a different colour — Red, Blue, Green, White and Pink. B lives on the top floor. Only one person lives between B and A. D likes Blue and lives immediately below B. C lives on a floor below E. E likes Red. The one who likes Green lives on an odd-numbered floor above A. A does not like White.

Which colour is liked by the person who lives on floor 1?
questions.explanation: B is on 5, D (Blue) on 4, A on 3; C below E gives C on 1 and E on 2. Green is on an odd floor above A → floor 5 (B). A is not White, so A is Pink and C is White.

questions.question:
Five persons A, B, C, D and E live on five different floors of a building (floor 1 is the bottom, floor 5 the top), and each likes a different colour — Red, Blue, Green, White and Pink. B lives on the top floor. Only one person lives between B and A. D likes Blue and lives immediately below B. C lives on a floor below E. E likes Red. The one who likes Green lives on an odd-numbered floor above A. A does not like White.

How many persons live between C and D?
questions.explanation: Floors 1→5: C, E, A, D, B. Between C (1) and D (4) are E and A — two persons.

questions.question: Five persons P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. Q sits at the extreme right end. S sits second to the left of Q. P sits immediately to the left of S. R does not sit at the extreme left end. Who sits in the middle of the row?
questions.explanation: Positions 1–5: Q = 5, S = 3, P = 2; R is not at 1, so R = 4 and T = 1. S is in the middle.

questions.question:
Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red.
Conclusions: I. Some roses are red. II. All flowers are roses.
questions.explanation: The red flowers need not include roses, and roses are only a part of flowers. Neither conclusion follows.

questions.question:
Statements: No laptop is a phone. Some phones are tablets.
Conclusions: I. Some tablets are not laptops. II. Some laptops are tablets.
questions.explanation: The tablets that are phones cannot be laptops, so I follows. II is only a possibility.

questions.question:
Statement: P < Q = R ≤ S < T
Conclusions: I. T > Q  II. P < S
questions.explanation: T > S ≥ R = Q gives T > Q; P < Q = R ≤ S gives P < S. Both follow.

questions.question:
Statements: K ≥ L > M; N ≥ L; O < M
Conclusions: I. N > O  II. K > N
questions.explanation: N ≥ L > M > O gives N > O. K and N are both ≥ L, so no relation between them. Only I follows.

questions.question: If 'MANGO' is coded as 'OGNAM', how is 'APPLE' coded?
questions.explanation: The word is written in reverse: APPLE → ELPPA.

questions.question: In a code language, 'bank loan approved' is written as 'ra si te', 'loan is pending' as 'te po mu' and 'approved is final' as 'mu si ka'. What is the code for 'pending'?
questions.explanation: loan = te (1 & 2), approved = si (1 & 3), is = mu (2 & 3). In 'loan is pending', the remaining code po = pending.

questions.question: A is the father of B. C is the mother of A. How is C related to B?
questions.explanation: C is the mother of B's father, i.e. B's grandmother.

questions.question: Introducing a man, Neha said, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is Neha related to the man?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of Neha's mother is Neha herself, so Neha is the man's mother.

questions.question: Kiran starts from point X, walks 15 m east, turns left and walks 8 m, then turns left again and walks 15 m. How far and in which direction is she from X?
questions.explanation: East 15 → north 8 → west 15 brings her 8 m directly north of X.

questions.question: In a queue, Amit is 12th from the front and Sunil is 18th from the back. Exactly four persons stand between them. What is the maximum possible number of persons in the queue?
questions.explanation: Maximum when Amit is ahead of Sunil with 4 persons between: 12 + 4 + 18 = 34.

questions.question: Find the next term: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +1 (A, B, C, D, E); second letters move −1 (Z, Y, X, W, V): EV.

questions.question:
Arrangement: R 4 T # 8 L @ 2 M 6 % N 9 & P 3 K
How many numbers are immediately followed by a symbol?
questions.explanation: Only 6 (followed by %) and 9 (followed by &) qualify — two.

questions.question: How many pairs of letters in the word 'CAPITAL' have as many letters between them in the word as in the English alphabet (in either direction)?
questions.explanation: P–L (3 letters between in both: I, T, A and M, N, O) and I–L (2 between: T, A and J, K). Two pairs.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: Square, Rectangle, Rhombus, Triangle, Parallelogram
questions.explanation: All others are quadrilaterals; a triangle has three sides.
